title: Choose the visual world for Project Journal
question: The roll assigned The Lined Script. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Lined Script
options.lineage: A film script supervisor's lined shooting script and daily continuity log
options.thesis: Each project is a shooting script; coloured pencil coverage lines in the margin show who did each part.
materials: screenplay pages in industry revision colours (white, blue, pink, yellow)
options.viewport: A chapter opens as a script page: scene number in both margins, a typed slugline, beginner prose, and pencil lines down the right margin for Claude, You or Together.
options.risk: Script supervision is a niche craft; if the pencil-line legend is not taught on the first page, the margins read as decoration.

raised.raise: Nothing is boxed: no cards anywhere; hierarchy lives only in margin position, typed sluglines and pencil lines.
A folded tape flag marks the scene you stopped reading and is re-flagged when you return.
One alarm colour, tally-light red, is reserved for irreversible moments (going live, deleting); nothing else may use it.
Every timeline take carries its real running time from git, right-aligned like a tracklist.
Evidence is graded by line style: straight pencil = witnessed in the conversation, squiggle = reconstructed from specs and commits.

options.label: The MRT Line Map
options.thesis: Each project is a rail network: Claude, You and Others run as coloured lines, Together is an interchange, chapters are stations.
options.viewport: The timeline as a horizontal line diagram, lanes as coloured routes that merge at interchange stations; chapters as stops you ride in order.
options.risk: Transit-map timelines are a familiar device; it is where many runs in this category land, and long prose has no native home on a map.

options.label: Brick Build Instructions
options.thesis: Every chapter is a numbered build step: what already exists is ghosted, the new piece arrives bright with an arrow to its seat.
options.viewport: Step 12 in huge numerals, a 1:1 parts call-out (e.g. 'GitHub Action, 1x'), and the system diagram with only the new piece in colour.
options.case: Fuses well and wins on recognisability for a beginner; loses on the core timeline, since instruction books never say who placed which piece.
options.risk: Can read toy-like, and long explanations fight a mostly wordless form.

options.label: Provenance Ribbon
options.thesis: One ribbon passes between hands through the project's life.
options.viewport: A single custody ribbon down the page with dated folds.
options.case: Its known/inferred distinction is exactly right, but a beginner coder does not identify with museum custody records.
options.kept: Evidence graded by line style (witnessed vs reconstructed).
options.risk: Reads archival and solemn for a learning notebook.

options.label: Cutting Bench Select Rail
options.thesis: Chapters as frames on a perforated rail; set-aside attempts hang on pins.
options.viewport: A rail of chapter frames across the top, tape flag where you stopped.
options.case: Same film family as the roll but weaker on who-did-what, and a black/orange field is hard for long reading.
options.kept: The tape flag that remembers where you stopped.
options.risk: Dark, dense field tires readers on long chapters.

options.label: Mixtape J-Card
options.thesis: Side A the redesign, Side B the admin, each track timed.
options.viewport: A folded tracklist with running times.
options.case: Charming for Loft Concept's two halves, but future projects will not split into two sides.
options.kept: Real running times right-aligned on every entry.

options.label: Penny-press Broadside
options.thesis: Each project shouted as one dense printed sheet.
options.viewport: Wood-type headline over two rammed columns.
options.case: Dense justified columns are the opposite of beginner-friendly reading.
options.kept: One alarm colour reserved for a single kind of moment.

options.label: Cracktro Scroller
options.thesis: Bitmap text on a drifting starfield, rank as depth.
options.viewport: One still line of text over drifting layers.
options.case: Bitmap text on black fails long-form beginner reading on a phone.
options.kept: Nothing enclosed by boxes; one consistent hierarchy mechanism.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean developer-docs site (left chapter sidebar, centred prose, right 'on this page' list), executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar of chapters, article column, a vertical timeline with filter chips.
canonCard.risk: This is the 'generic docs template' you said would feel wrong.
